lines.text: Auto approval is wonderful for safe, repetitive work. But it is not a switch for the whole world.
Formatting, lint fixes and docs edits are fine. They are local, and you can undo them in one command.
Deploys, deletes and anything with money are different. A wrong call there cannot be taken back.
For that work, you want the question. The agent stops, and a human says yes or no.
So YOLO is set per task. The lint sweep gets it, and the deploy task does not.
Or set it per workspace. A docs workspace can run free, and a billing workspace never does.
Keep risky work in a workspace or task that never has YOLO. Then a slip of the finger cannot reach it.
Even with YOLO on, every call stays in the tool call history, so you can check afterwards.
Skim the history after a run. If something looks odd, you catch it while it is still small.
And if a task starts to feel risky, switch YOLO off in the middle, and the questions return at once.
Start small. Give YOLO to one safe task, watch the history, and widen it only as trust grows.
You decide where trust is earned. Try YOLO mode at Agent R Q dot com.
